problemText: In 480 BCE a Greek fleet led by Athens trapped and destroyed the Persian navy in a narrow strait, ending Persia's second invasion of Greece. Which battle is this?
choices: Marathon
Salamis
Thermopylae
Chaeronea
hints: Sort the choices by what kind of fighting each involved: one was a land battle on a plain in 490 BCE, one a stand at a mountain pass, one a Macedonian victory in 338 BCE, and one a fleet action.

problemText: Corinth, Thebes, and Argos each had its own laws, army, coins, and religious festivals, while all three shared the Greek language, the poems of Homer, and the Olympic Games. What is the term for one of these independent communities?
choices: A province administered by a single Greek king
A colony held permanently under Athenian rule
A polis, an independent city-state with its own government, laws, and army
A satrapy governed by an appointee of the Persian king
hints: The question describes people who shared a culture but not a government. Which word names the unit of government rather than the shared culture?

problemText: Spartan decisions were made by two hereditary kings, a council of elders, and five overseers called ephors. Which label best describes this system?
choices: A direct democracy in which citizens personally voted on every law
A representative democracy in which citizens elected officials to vote on laws for them
A monarchy in which one hereditary king held absolute power
An oligarchy, with political power concentrated in the hands of a small number of men
hints: Count the people who actually cast the deciding votes, and check how many kings Sparta had.

problemText: After the Persian invasions, allied Greek cities increasingly paid Athens cash instead of contributing warships. Athens moved the alliance treasury to Athens, spent from it on its own building projects, and used force against members that tried to withdraw. Which consequence does this best explain?
choices: A defensive alliance turned into an Athenian empire, and Spartan fear of that growing power helped bring on the Peloponnesian War
Persia recovered control of the Aegean and forced the Greek cities back under its rule
Athens abandoned its navy and rebuilt its power around a land army modeled on Sparta's
The member cities merged with Athens into a single unified Greek kingdom with one shared citizenship
hints: Trace two things: who controls the money, and what happens to a member that wants to leave.

problemText: An Athenian writer of the 400s BCE remarked, in paraphrase: 'Among us even a man who owns no land may rise and speak in the Assembly, and may be chosen by lot to judge cases on a jury.' Which use of this passage as evidence is most defensible?
choices: Evidence that every adult living in Athens, including women and enslaved residents, could vote in the Assembly
Evidence that Athens had replaced voting in person with the election of representatives who voted on citizens' behalf
Evidence that Athenian public office was reserved for wealthy landowners, as seats on Sparta's council of elders were
Evidence that political rights among Athenian citizens did not depend on wealth, though women, enslaved people, and resident foreigners were not citizens at all
hints: Ask the passage two separate questions: what it shows about citizens, and how many residents of Athens counted as citizens in the first place.

problemText: A student reasons: 'Sparta defeated Athens in 404 BCE, so Sparta must have been the dominant power in Greece when Philip II of Macedon took control at Chaeronea in 338 BCE.' Which correction is best supported by the evidence?
choices: Sparta never fought the Peloponnesian War; Persia defeated Athens directly and then withdrew from Greece
Philip II had already conquered Greece before the Peloponnesian War began, so Sparta's victory changed nothing
Twenty-seven years of war drained every major polis, the victor included, so Spartan dominance proved brief and it was the exhaustion of the Greek states that let Macedon take control
Sparta's victory left it so powerful that Macedon was never able to gain control of the Greek mainland
hints: Winning a long war and emerging stronger from it are not the same thing. Check the condition of the winner, not just the result.
Line up the dates: the war ran 431 to 404 BCE and Chaeronea came in 338 BCE. Ask what happened to Greek military strength in the decades between.

problemText: Historians use one term for the roughly two-hundred-year stretch of internal peace, road building, and long-distance trade that began with the rule of Augustus. What is that term?
choices: Pax Romana
The Conflict of the Orders
The Punic Wars
The Hellenistic Age
hints: The phrase is Latin and means, literally, 'Roman peace.'

problemText: Around 450 BCE, under pressure from the plebeians, Roman law was written down and posted publicly as the Twelve Tables. Why did plebeians want the law written and displayed?
choices: Written, publicly displayed law meant patrician officials could no longer decide cases by rules only they knew
It gave the plebeians a permanent majority in the Senate
It abolished the office of consul and replaced it with a single elected king
It ended slavery throughout Roman territory
hints: Ask what changes for an ordinary person the moment a rule is posted where anyone can read it.

problemText: The Roman Republic elected two consuls every year, each able to block the other's decisions, and each holding the office for only one year. What was the purpose of that arrangement?
choices: To speed up decision-making by removing checks on officials
To keep any single man from accumulating the permanent, unchecked power of a king
To transfer lawmaking directly to an assembly open to all residents, including non-citizens
To guarantee that patricians and plebeians owned equal amounts of land
hints: Two seats, mutual blocking, and a one-year term are three limits pointed at the same danger. Name the danger.

problemText: Victory over Carthage in the Punic Wars brought Rome vast conquered land and enormous numbers of enslaved captives, and wealthy Romans combined both into giant estates. Which consequence for the republic followed most directly?
choices: Rome's population collapsed so sharply that the Senate abolished taxation
Carthage recovered and annexed Rome's territories in Italy
The Senate granted full citizenship to the enslaved laborers working the new estates
Small citizen-farmers could not compete, lost their land, and moved into the city, eroding the landowning base from which the army had traditionally been recruited
hints: Follow the small farmer out of the countryside, then ask what property qualification army service used to require.

problemText: A Roman writer looking back on his own era summarized it this way, in paraphrase: 'The state, worn out by long years of civil war, passed under the control of one man, who took the title of first citizen and refused the name of king.' Which development does this describe?
choices: The expulsion of Rome's last king and the creation of two annually elected consuls
The end of republican government in one-man rule that kept republican titles and offices as a familiar covering
The plebeian victory in the Conflict of the Orders, which won commoners the office of tribune
The permanent division of the empire into eastern and western halves ruled from two capitals
hints: Both halves of the sentence matter: exhaustion from civil war, and a ruler who takes real power while avoiding the word 'king.'

problemText: A student writes: 'Rome fell in 476 CE, which is when Augustus ended the republic.' Which sequence correctly separates the events the student has collapsed together?
choices: Augustus deposed the last western emperor in 476 CE, and the republic continued in the east until 1453
The western empire fell in 476 CE, after which the republic was restored in the east and lasted until 1453
The republic ended in 27 BCE when Augustus took power; the western empire ended in 476 CE; the eastern empire, ruled from Constantinople, lasted until 1453
The republic and the western empire both ended in 476 CE, and no Roman state existed anywhere after that year
hints: Separate 'a government changing its form' from 'a state ceasing to exist.' They are different kinds of event and they happen in different centuries.
Three endings, three dates: one in the first century BCE, one in the fifth century CE, one in the fifteenth century CE.

problemText: Which Mauryan emperor had moral instructions carved on rocks and pillars across his empire and sent Buddhist missionaries as far as Sri Lanka?
choices: Chandragupta Maurya
Ashoka
Shi Huangdi
Aryabhata
hints: He was the grandson of the man who founded the Maurya empire around 321 BCE.

problemText: The Qin governed on the principle that people naturally pursue their own interest, so order must come from uniform written law and severe punishment rather than from the ruler's moral example. What is this governing philosophy called?
choices: Confucianism
Daoism
Legalism
Filial piety
hints: Two of the choices describe governing by personal virtue or by harmony with nature. Find the one that names a doctrine of strict, uniform law.

problemText: Chinese political thought held that heaven granted the right to rule to a just dynasty and withdrew it from a corrupt one, so that a successful rebellion was read as proof the right had passed. What did this idea, the Mandate of Heaven, make possible?
choices: It made the emperor a living god whose actions could not be judged by anyone
It required every government post to be inherited from father to son
It forbade any change of dynasty, since heaven's choice was understood to be permanent
It supplied a standard for judging a dynasty legitimate, and therefore a way to justify overthrowing one that ruled badly
hints: Ask what this idea lets a rebel say about a dynasty that is losing wars, raising taxes, and suffering famine.

problemText: Emperor Wudi founded an imperial university in 124 BCE, and the Han increasingly selected officials through written examinations on the Confucian classics. Which statement best describes the effect of that policy?
choices: Government posts went increasingly to men trained in a shared body of texts rather than to hereditary nobles alone, though the years of study required wealth that most families never had
Every family in China gained an equal chance at high office, ending inequality in Han society
The Han abandoned the centralized administration inherited from the Qin and returned power to independent regional kingdoms
Officials were selected by lottery from among all adult men, as jurors were in Athens
hints: Two things change at once here: who is eligible in principle, and who can afford the years of preparation in practice. A good answer holds both.

problemText: One of Ashoka's carved messages reads, in paraphrase: 'Whoever praises his own tradition and condemns another's does the greatest harm to his own; let people instead listen to one another's teachings.' What does this inscription best support as evidence?
choices: That Buddhism was the only religion permitted in the Maurya empire and all others were banned

That the emperor publicly promoted respect among his subjects' different traditions and used state monuments to broadcast policy, which is evidence of official messaging rather than proof of everyday practice
That Ashoka had disbanded his army and returned the territory he had taken at Kalinga
That Maurya subjects voted in public assemblies to decide which teachings the empire would support
hints: Ask who commissioned the text and where it was placed before asking whether it describes how people actually behaved.

problemText: A student writes: 'The Han, the western Roman, and the Gupta empires all ended for the same single reason, which is that invaders came from outside.' Which assessment of that claim is best supported?
choices: Invasion played no role in any of the three cases; each empire failed purely from internal problems
All three empires fell within the same decade, which proves that one shared external cause was responsible
Each empire ended peacefully when its ruling family chose to divide its territory among regional heirs

Frontier pressure was real in all three cases, but each state was already strained by unaffordable military costs, factional infighting at court, tax pressure on farmers, and epidemics moving along its own trade routes, so invasion finished off states weakened from within
hints: Ask whether the outside pressure was new, or whether it succeeded against a state that had already been weakened.
Check the dates as well: the Han broke apart in 220 CE, the western Roman Empire in 476 CE, and the Gupta empire around 550 CE. That is three centuries apart, not one shared moment.

problemText: Which teacher, born in the region of present-day Nepal and northern India in roughly the 500s BCE, taught the Four Noble Truths and the Eightfold Path?
choices: Confucius
Laozi
Siddhartha Gautama
Ashoka
hints: The title 'Buddha' means 'the awakened one' and was given to this teacher; it was not his birth name.

problemText: Confucius taught that a stable society rests on five relationships, ruler and subject, parent and child, husband and wife, elder and younger sibling, and friend and friend, each carrying duties that run in both directions. Which statement best describes this teaching?
choices: It locates social order in reciprocal moral obligations between people rather than in enforcement by harsh law
It requires subjects to obey rulers who owe them nothing in return
It urges people to withdraw from society and live in solitary harmony with nature
It describes duties owed to a creator god rather than to other human beings
hints: The phrase 'in both directions' is doing real work here. Ask whether the superior in each pair is also bound by duties.

problemText: Judaism taught belief in a single God at a time when most neighboring peoples honored many, described a covenant, or binding agreement, between God and the people, and preserved a written law, the Torah, understood to apply to rulers as well as to ordinary people. Which pair of features does this describe?
choices: Polytheism paired with rituals reserved to a hereditary priestly caste
A belief that rulers are themselves divine and therefore stand above the law
Monotheism paired with a covenant and a written law understood to bind everyone, rulers included
A tradition with no scripture at all, in which a ruler's decrees supplied the only rules
hints: Answer two questions in order: how many gods does the tradition describe, and who is the written law said to apply to?

problemText: After the Han dynasty broke apart in 220 CE, Buddhism gained large numbers of followers in China, and the Mahayana forms that grew there left room for honoring ancestors and meeting family obligations. Which explanation best accounts for that growth?
choices: Indian armies conquered northern China and required the population to convert
A long period of political disorder made existing answers look inadequate, and a form of the teaching that accommodated ancestral and family duties lowered the cost of adopting it
Han emperors had made Buddhism the official state religion in 124 BCE, so its later growth was simply enforced from above
Its appeal lay in requiring converts to abandon family obligations entirely, which Chinese families welcomed
hints: The question supplies two clues: when the growth happened, and what the teaching did not ask people to give up.

problemText: An ancient Chinese text advises, in paraphrase: 'The best ruler is barely noticed by the people. He does least and forces least, and when the work is finished the people say they did it themselves.' Which tradition does this reflect, and what claim about power is it making?
choices: Legalism, holding that order comes from detailed uniform law backed by severe punishment
Confucianism, holding that a ruler should actively instruct subjects in ritual and correct conduct
Judaism, holding that a ruler's authority rests on a covenant between God and the people
Daoism, holding that the ideal is wu wei, effortless action, so that order arises from working with the natural way rather than straining against it
hints: The advice praises doing less rather than doing more correctly. Ask which of these traditions treats forcing itself as the problem.

problemText: Which statement most accurately compares Hinduism and Buddhism as they developed in South Asia?
choices: Both use the vocabulary of karma, dharma, and rebirth, but Hinduism developed over many centuries with no single founder, founding moment, or single scripture, while Buddhism began with a specific human teacher who set aside priestly ritual authority and birth-based spiritual standing
Buddhism is simply a later name for Hinduism, and the two have always been one tradition under two labels
Hinduism began with a single founder in the 500s BCE, while Buddhism accumulated gradually over more than a thousand years with no founder
The two share no vocabulary or concepts, having developed in unrelated regions and periods
hints: Separate shared vocabulary from shared structure. Two traditions can use the same words and still be built in different ways.
Ask the same three questions of each tradition: is there a founder, is there a founding moment, and is there one scripture?
